text:
alex: heads up — we've seen a growing chunk of traces with no service-level trace id after the mobile->edge proxy rollout. cost attribution drops for those requests. want to sync on short-term stitch heuristics vs longer-term contract changes :wave:

maria: how big is "growing"? any numbers?

alex: roughly: last 7d ingestion shows 6.1% of completed requests missing billing_key or root-trace-id; up from ~1.2% before proxy change. impact concentrated on mobile sdk clients and a few legacy partners.

kevin: is the missing id because proxies strip headers? can we add header passthrough?

alex: proxies are doing some header normalization and our header (x-rw-trace-id) wasn't whitelisted by the partner proxy. partner unwilling to change policy for now.

sam: quick idea: stitch at enrichment using deterministic fingerprinting (ip + ua + path + 10s window) hashed. cheap to implement.

ana: careful — ip+ua is high cardinality and may be PII depending on IP retention rules. also mobile NAT means ip isn't stable, could stitch wrong user across sessions.

kevin: agree with ana. also fingerprint will reduce precision and create false positives; could screw chargeback.

maria: what about probabilistic stitch + confidence score? we only apply attribution if confidence > 0.9, otherwise mark as "best_effort" and don't charge-back to teams.

obs-bot: incident-bot: 1767001300 - sampling-alert - sampling rate changed for mobile pipeline -> 2x to compensate upstream undercounting.

alex: thanks obs-bot. plan I'm leaning to: short-term (weeks) implement an enrichment-stage "stitcher":
- only use telemetry that is privacy-safe (hashed path + hour-bucket + sdk_version)
- limit to 30s window
- emit a new field stitch_confidence: LOW|MED|HIGH
- do NOT mutate billing_key; instead write derived_billing_hint for downstream billing glue jobs

kevin: derived_billing_hint is smart — keeps original data intact and gives billing teams a handle to accept/reject stitch matches.

sam: ok but we need explicit opt-out and a metric to measure false-positive rate. propose canary 5% traffic with stitch enabled and separate metric counters: stitched_ok, stitch_conflicts, stitch_ambiguous.

ana: agree. also add a privacy review: what salt/hash we use, retention for derived hints, and ensure HSM-backed salt rotation if we store anything reversible (we won't).

maria: longer-term: update ingest contract to include optional client_trace_token (sdk-generated short id) that survives proxies (put into envelope, not header). SDK+partners adopt over months. that gives us deterministic linking without heuristics.

alex: timeline proposal:
- t+1 week: implement lightweight stitcher prototype in enrichment (no billing acceptance, just metrics), instrument stitched_ok/conflict/ambiguous
- t+3 weeks: privacy review + opt-out flag + 5% canary where derived_billing_hint is surfaced to billing pipeline in read-only mode
- t+8 weeks: expand canary to 25% if FP within threshold (<0.5%), implement acceptance path to use derived hints for internal cost dashboards
- t+12-20 weeks: SDK & partner rollouts for client_trace_token + contract bump to require optional token in envelope

kevin: what threshold for false positives? 0.5% overall seems tight. maybe set target on business-impact: stitched attribution should not change per-team cost by >0.2% month-over-month.

sam: +1 to business-impact metric. also add a manual override endpoint for billing owners to mark a stitch as invalid and feed back into classifier.

ana: add retention policy: derived_billing_hint stored for 7 days in enrichment store, persisted in cold storage for 30 days for audits, then deleted. need legal signoff.

maria: rollout owners: alex -> stitcher implementation; sam -> metrics & canary infra; kevin -> billing integration; ana -> privacy review. I'll coordinate partner comms.

alex: one open design question — do we expose stitch_confidence to downstream quota/rls decisions? my vote: no for now. only for observability and billing hinting.

kevin: agree. do not use for quota decisions until super low false-positive rate and proven non-abusive.

sam: dev checklist: unit tests for hash determinism, load test for enrichment CPU overhead (target <5% p95 increase), feature flag gating, and a debug logging mode to record sample raw inputs (PII scrubbed) for labeling.

ana: privacy checklist: HMAC with rotating salt, salt rotation doc, no raw IPs persisted, opt-out honor, update privacy policy blurbs, get legal + sec ack before canary expansion.

maria: i'll create a small RFC doc and a short partner note template. can we aim to start the prototype next week?

alex: yes — starting Monday. i'll post wd progress updates here. thanks all :thumbsup: 

kevin: cool. one last ask — add a dashboard tile that shows "percent requests with billing_key" and "percent attributed via stitch" side-by-side. helps ops and biz teams see progress.

sam: i'll own the dashboard.

obs-bot: reminder: create incident/ops playbook item for when stitcher causes unexpected billing swings.

alex: noted. end state: graceful fallback from heuristics to deterministic client_trace_token with privacy-safe defaults and clear owner ops runbook.

maria: great — moving to action items now.
